mainTopic: The form of הבדלה, how שבת sets a meal for קידוש but not for הבדלה, what may be eaten or drunk before הבדלה, and making up a missed קידוש
overview: The גמרא first defends עולא, who said הבדלה with no closing ברכה. It explains that הבדלה is like a ברכת המצוות: both are pure praise, so neither needs a closing. Next comes a story. The students of רב were eating as שבת began, and רב המנונא סבא told them they did not need to restart their meal, because שבת sets the meal by itself, just as it does for מעשר. רב עמרם adds that this is true for קידוש but not for הבדלה, so a meal may continue after שבת ends. The גמרא then limits this: you may continue a meal but not start one, and you must stop drinking wine or beer, though water is allowed. רב הונא disagrees and is strict even about water, based on a teaching of רבי עקיבא, while the scholars of רב אשי were lenient. Finally, רב נחמן בר יצחק rules that a missed Friday-night קידוש may be made the next day, learning it from a missed הבדלה. רבינא challenges this from a ברייתא and is answered, then begins a second challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A challenge to עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the source just quoted is difficult for עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is difficult for עולא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that what it just learned contradicts עולא, who said הבדלה without a closing 'ברוך' ending. This line sets up the defense that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source just quoted implies that a longer ברכה like הבדלה should open with 'ברוך' and also close with 'ברוך'. עולא only opened with 'ברוך' and gave no closing, so his practice seems to clash with that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a challenge that is left standing for now
An אמורא whose way of saying הבדלה is being questioned

phrases.english: It is difficult for Ulla!
phrases.notes: עולא opened הבדלה with 'ברוך' but did not close it with 'ברוך'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion earlier about how הבדלה is phrased and ended.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's practice of saying הבדלה without a closing ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source just cited implies that הבדלה needs a closing 'ברוך', and עולא left it out.

steps.title: הבדלה is like a blessing over a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: עולא would answer that הבדלה is in the same class as a ברכת המצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא could say to you: this blessing is also like a blessing over מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by putting הבדלה in the same group as the ברכות said before doing a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכת המצוות, such as the ברכה before lighting candles, has only one 'ברוך' at the start and no closing. If הבדלה belongs to that group, it also needs no closing, so עולא is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you; introduces a defense on someone's behalf
A ברכה said before doing a מצוה
It is similar to; it belongs to the same group

phrases.english: Ulla could say to you:
this too is like a blessing over מצוות,
phrases.notes: So it only needs an opening 'Blessed', not a closing one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: הבדלה is placed in the group of ברכות המצוות, which have no closing ברכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הבדלה is a longer ברכה that needs a closing 'ברוך'
steps.terutzMaskana: הבדלה works like a ברכת המצוות and needs no closing

steps.title: Why do מצוה blessings have no closing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is that ברכות המצוות need no closing ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for blessings over מצוות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask why ברכות המצוות need no closing. This sets up the explanation that shows why הבדלה fits the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing two things only works if we know the reason behind the rule. Once we know why ברכות המצוות have no closing, we can check whether that reason also applies to הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Blessings over מצוות, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why don't they need a closing blessing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the comparison made in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason ברכות המצוות do not need a closing ברכה

steps.title: Because they are pure praise, and so is הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: ברכות המצוות are pure praise, and הבדלה is also pure praise, so neither needs a closing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is praise. This, too, is praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: a ברכת המצוות is simply a הודאה, praise of הקב"ה, and הבדלה is also simply praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A closing ברכה is needed when a ברכה includes more than praise, such as requests. Pure praise needs no closing, and since הבדלה is only praise, עולא's practice is justified.

keyTerms.meaning: Praise or thanks to הקב"ה
Because

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's short הבדלה with no closing ברכה is defended. Like a ברכת המצוות, הבדלה is pure הודאה, and pure praise needs no closing.

phrases.english: Because it is praise —
this, too, is praise.
phrases.notes: הבדלה is also pure praise, so it also needs no closing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3 and completes the defense of עולא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ברכות המצוות are pure הודאה, and so is הבדלה, so no closing is needed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge to עולא is resolved.

steps.title: The students ask whether to restart their meal for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The students of רב, eating as Shabbat approached, sent רב המנונא סבא to check whether Shabbat had begun so they could stop and restart the meal for Shabbat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניא בר שלמיא and the students of רב were sitting at a meal, and רב המנונא סבא was standing over them, serving. They said to him: Go see whether the day has become holy. If so, we will stop and set the meal for Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. The students think that if Shabbat starts during their meal, they must stop and formally restart it as a Shabbat meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their assumption is that a meal begun on a weekday stays a weekday meal unless they actively stop it and 'set' it again for Shabbat. The rest of the sugya tests this assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal
The day has become holy, meaning Shabbat has begun
We will stop or interrupt
We will set or establish it

phrases.aramaic: רַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא וְתַלְמִידֵי דְּרַב
phrases.english: Rav Ḥananya bar Shelemya and the students of Rav
were sitting at a meal,
and Rav Hamnuna the Elder was standing over them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: זִיל חֲזִי אִי מִקְּדִישׁ יוֹמָא
phrases.english: They said to him: Go see if the day has become sanctified,
and we will stop and set it for Shabbat.
phrases.notes: For example, by removing the table and bringing it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא וְתַלְמִידֵי דְּרַב הֲווֹ יָתְבִי בִּסְעוֹדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a meal that runs into Shabbat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students assume a meal must be actively restarted to become a Shabbat meal.

steps.title: שבת sets the meal by itself
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא סבא tells them they do not need to stop, because Shabbat sets the meal on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You do not need to. Shabbat sets itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא סבא answers that no action is needed, because once Shabbat starts, the meal automatically becomes a Shabbat meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rejects the students' assumption from step 5. Shabbat does not wait for anyone to set the meal; its arrival does it automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: You do not need to
It sets itself; it establishes things on its own

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this means they can keep eating without קידוש. It means only that they do not need a special act, like removing the table, to make the meal a Shabbat meal.

phrases.english: He said to them: You do not need to —
Shabbat establishes itself.
phrases.notes: Whatever is eaten after nightfall is automatically part of the Shabbat meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the students' plan in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no need to stop and restart the meal, because Shabbat sets it on its own.

steps.title: רב's rule: שבת sets the meal for מעשר and for קידוש
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא סבא's source is רב's rule that Shabbat sets the meal for מעשר and also for קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב said: Just as Shabbat sets the meal for מעשר, so Shabbat sets it for קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רב המנונא סבא's answer: a statement of רב comparing קידוש to מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person may snack on produce that has not had מעשר taken, as long as it is not a fixed meal. On Shabbat, though, all eating counts as fixed, so מעשר must be taken first. In the same way, Shabbat automatically creates the קידוש obligation, which shows that the meal has become a Shabbat meal without any action.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets or establishes; turns eating into a fixed meal or creates an obligation
Tithes that must be separated from produce
The ברכה that declares Shabbat holy
Just as... so too

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that a meal which runs into שבת becomes a שבת meal automatically. The person must make קידוש, but does not need to restart the meal.

phrases.english: As Rav said:
Just as Shabbat establishes for tithes,
phrases.notes: On שבת, even casual eating counts as a fixed meal, so מעשר must be taken first.

phrases.english: so Shabbat establishes for kiddush.
phrases.notes: Once שבת begins, one may not continue eating without קידוש.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַשַּׁבָּת קוֹבַעַת לְמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: Shabbat sets the meal by itself
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב: Shabbat קובעת for מעשר and for קידוש

steps.title: The students assume the same applies to הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The students conclude that the end of Shabbat must likewise set the meal for הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this that just as Shabbat sets the meal for קידוש, so it sets the meal for הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The students stretch רב's rule to the end of Shabbat. This is an assumption that is about to be corrected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this were true, a meal still going on when Shabbat ends would have to stop for הבדלה, and the rest of it would no longer count as a Shabbat meal. The next step shows that this extension is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it; often an assumption that will be corrected
The ברכה that separates Shabbat from the weekday

phrases.english: They understood from it
that just as it establishes for kiddush,
so it establishes for havdala,
phrases.notes: Meaning one would have to stop the meal for הבדלה when שבת ends.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבוּר מִינַּהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּקָבְעָה לְקִידּוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further conclusion from רב's rule in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students' assumption: Shabbat's end sets the meal for הבדלה, just as its start sets it for קידוש.

steps.title: רב עמרם: קידוש yes, הבדלה no
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם reports that רב said Shabbat sets the meal for קידוש but not for הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said to them: This is what רב said: Shabbat sets the meal for קידוש, but it does not set it for הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם corrects the students' assumption by quoting רב's exact words, which limit the rule to קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shabbat's arrival forces a stop for קידוש, but Shabbat's departure does not force a stop for הבדלה. A person may finish a meal that continues past the end of Shabbat and say הבדלה afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he said; introduces an exact quote that corrects a misunderstanding
The אמורא who reports רב's precise wording

steps.whatToRemember: Shabbat sets a meal automatically for קידוש, so there is no need to restart it, but קידוש must be said. Shabbat does not do the same for הבדלה, so one may keep eating after Shabbat ends.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב עַמְרָם, הָכִי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Amram said to them: This is what Rav said:
It establishes for kiddush,
but it does not establish for havdala.
phrases.notes: There is no need to interrupt a meal for הבדלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב עַמְרָם, הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the students' assumption from step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects extending רב's rule to הבדלה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב's actual words limit the rule to קידוש only
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Shabbat sets the meal for קידוש but not for הבדלה.

steps.title: You may continue a meal, but not start one
steps.stepSummary: The rule of not stopping for הבדלה applies only to a meal already in progress. A new meal may not be started before הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule only means we don't have to stop a meal that is already going. But we may not start a new meal before הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the ruling from Step 9 that you don't have to stop your meal for הבדלה. It says this applies only to a meal that has already begun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 taught that Shabbat does not 'set' the meal for הבדלה, so you may keep eating. Here the גמרא adds a limit: that leniency covers only continuing. Starting to eat after Shabbat is over is still forbidden until you make הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to... (a limiting phrase)
To interrupt or stop
To begin or start

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first of three limits that together define exactly what is allowed before הבדלה.

phrases.english: And these words apply regarding interrupting
phrases.notes: Refers to Step 9: no need to stop the meal for הבדלה.

phrases.english: that we do not interrupt
but to begin, we do not begin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of רב's ruling from Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ongoing meal need not be stopped for הבדלה, but a new meal may not be started before הבדלה.

steps.title: Continuing is allowed only for eating, not drinking
steps.stepSummary: Only eating may continue past nightfall. Drinking must stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even the rule about not stopping applies only to eating. Someone who is drinking must stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule a second time. You may keep eating, but if you were only drinking, you must stop once Shabbat ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a meal is treated as significant, so it may continue. Drinking on its own is less weighty, so it gets no such allowance. Once night falls, drinking must wait for הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this about... (a limiting formula)
Eating
Drinking

phrases.english: And interrupting too, we only said
regarding eating;
but regarding drinking, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִיפְסָק נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בַּאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit on top of Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The allowance to continue past nightfall applies only to eating, not to drinking.

steps.title: The drinking restriction applies to wine and beer, not water
steps.stepSummary: Only significant drinks like wine and beer are forbidden before הבדלה. Water is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule about drinking applies only to wine and beer. Water is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third limit. The ban on drinking before הבדלה covers only important drinks, so water is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine and beer are respected, meal-like drinks, so drinking them before הבדלה is a problem. Water is not considered significant. According to this view, you may even start drinking water before הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine
Beer, or another strong drink
We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: Before הבדלה: you may continue eating a meal you already started, but you may not start one. You must stop drinking wine or beer. Water is permitted according to this view.

phrases.english: And drinking too, we only said
regarding wine and beer;
but water, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁתִיָּה נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּחַמְרָא וְשִׁיכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third limit, narrowing the drinking ban from Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water may be drunk before הבדלה; only wine and beer are restricted.

steps.title: רב הונא disagrees and warns a man about drinking water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב הונא disagrees with Step 12. He scolded a man for drinking water before הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רב הונא. רב הונא once saw a man drinking water before הבדלה and asked him: Aren't you afraid of the deadly illness אסכרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the leniency about water conflicts with רב הונא's view. It tells a story in which רב הונא warned a man who drank water before הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 allowed water before הבדלה. רב הונא's reaction shows he held that even water is forbidden. This is not a full refutation; it shows that two opinions exist.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees with...
A deadly throat illness, such as diphtheria or croup

phrases.english: And this disagrees with רב הונא.
For רב הונא saw a certain man
who drank water before הבדלה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא מִיסְתְּפֵי מָר מֵאַסְכָּרָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is the master not afraid of askara?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to the water leniency in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in Step 12 that water is permitted before הבדלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא's warning shows that he forbade even water before הבדלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא held that even water may not be drunk before הבדלה, which disagrees with the leniency in Step 12.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: whoever tastes anything before הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's source is a teaching from רבי עקיבא that anyone who tastes anything before הבדלה will die of אסכרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it was taught in the name of רבי עקיבא: anyone who tastes anything before making הבדלה will die from אסכרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source behind רב הונא's warning. It is a ברייתא in the name of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'anything' (כלום). Nothing is excluded, so water is included too. That is why רב הונא was strict even about water.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Anything at all
His death

phrases.english: As it was taught in the name of רבי עקיבא:
Anyone who tastes anything before he makes הבדלה,
his death is through askara.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב הונא's warning in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that even water is forbidden before הבדלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of רבי עקיבא: 'anyone who tastes anything' before הבדלה dies of אסכרה.

steps.title: רב אשי's school was not strict about water
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of רב אשי's academy were not particular about drinking water before הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis of רב אשי's academy were not strict about water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the water discussion by reporting what the scholars of רב אשי's school actually did. They were not concerned about drinking water before הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This practice sides with the leniency of Step 12 against רב הונא. In practice, the scholars were not strict about water, and their restriction applied to significant drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of רב אשי's academy
Were particular or strict
Water

steps.whatToRemember: There is a dispute about drinking water before הבדלה. רב הונא was strict, based on רבי עקיבא. רב אשי's school was lenient.

phrases.english: The rabbis of the house of Rav Ashi
were not particular about water.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי לָא קָפְדִי אַמַּיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a practice that supports the leniency of Step 12 over רב הונא's view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, רב אשי's school was not strict about drinking water before הבדלה.

steps.title: Can a missed Friday-night קידוש be made up the next day?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב נחמן בר יצחק whether someone who did not make קידוש on Friday night can make it during Shabbat day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked רב נחמן בר יצחק: If someone did not make קידוש on Friday night, may he make it any time during the whole next day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question from רבינא. Its answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proper time for קידוש is Friday night, when Shabbat begins. The question is whether missing that time means losing the מצוה completely, or whether it can still be done on Shabbat day.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a formal question)
Here: Friday night, the start of Shabbat
And continues, meaning he may do it at any point

steps.confusionAlert: Here עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת means Friday night, the beginning of Shabbat. It does not mean Friday afternoon.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבִינָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Ravina asked of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
One who did not make kiddush on Shabbat eve,
what is the law, may he go on to make kiddush
the entire day?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבִינָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about making up a missed קידוש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a missed Friday-night קידוש may be recited during Shabbat day.

steps.title: Yes, learned from the rule about a missed הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that קידוש may be made all day. He learns this from the sons of רבי חייא, who allow a missed הבדלה to be made during the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: The sons of רבי חייא said that someone who did not make הבדלה on Saturday night may make it during the whole week. So here too, someone who did not make קידוש on Friday night may make it all day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers רבינא's question by comparing קידוש to הבדלה. Since a missed הבדלה can be made up later, a missed קידוש can be made up too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons of רבי חייא ruled that הבדלה has an extended make-up period. רב נחמן בר יצחק infers from this that קידוש works the same way. Just as a missed הבדלה may be made later in the week, a missed קידוש may be made later on Shabbat day.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that they said
The sons of רבי חייא
Saturday night, after Shabbat ends
Here too (the same applies)

steps.confusionAlert: In 'כל השבת כולו' here, the word שבת means the whole week, not the day of Shabbat.
steps.whatToRemember: A missed קידוש may be made during Shabbat day, and a missed הבדלה may be made during the week. The קידוש ruling is learned from the הבדלה ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule that missing the ideal time for קידוש or הבדלה does not cancel the מצוה completely.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּאָמְרִי בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: He said to him: From the fact that the sons of Rabbi Chiya said:
One who did not make havdala at the conclusion of Shabbat
may go on to make havdala the entire week,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: מִי שֶׁלֹּא קִידֵּשׁ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: here too: one who did not make kiddush on Shabbat eve
may go on to make kiddush the entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּאָמְרִי בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A missed קידוש may be made all day, by comparison to the sons of רבי חייא's ruling that a missed הבדלה may be made all week.

steps.title: רבינא quotes a source about when there is קידוש over a cup
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a ברייתא: on the nights of שבת and יום טוב there is קידוש over a cup and a mention in ברכת המזון. During the day there is no קידוש over a cup, but there is still a mention in ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: On the nights of שבת and יום טוב there is קידוש over a cup, and there is a mention of the day in ברכת המזון. On שבת and יום טוב day there is no קידוש over a cup, but there is a mention in ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא quotes a ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן בר יצחק. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up two times, night and day. At night there are two things: קידוש over a cup and a mention in ברכת המזון. During the day there is only the mention in ברכת המזון, and the ברייתא says flatly that there is no קידוש over a cup.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from an older source)
קידוש said over a cup of wine
A mention of the special day (like רצה or יעלה ויבוא)
Grace after meals

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: לֵילֵי שַׁבָּת וְלֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: He objected to him: On the nights of Shabbat and the nights of Yom Tov
phrases.notes: רבינא objects to רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: there is Kiddush over a cup
and there is a mention of the day in Grace after Meals.
phrases.notes: רצה on שבת, יעלה ויבוא on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב — אֵין בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה עַל הַכּוֹס,
phrases.english: On Shabbat and Yom Tov day, there is no Kiddush over a cup,
but there is a mention in Grace after Meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to contradict the answer in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling that קידוש may be made all day long.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says there is no קידוש over a cup during the day, with no exceptions mentioned.

steps.title: Why the source contradicts making up קידוש by day
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains: if a missed קידוש could be made the next day, then there would be a case of קידוש over a cup on שבת day. So the ברייתא should not have said 'there is no קידוש over a cup' during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that someone who did not make קידוש on Friday night may make it all day long, then on שבת and יום טוב day there is also a case of קידוש over a cup: if he did not make קידוש at night, he makes it the next day!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא spells out the problem. Your ruling creates a daytime קידוש, but the ברייתא says there is none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, a person who forgot קידוש at night would say it by day. That is a real daytime קידוש over a cup. Yet the ברייתא clearly says that during the day there is none, so it seems to reject his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
He may keep making קידוש (any time)
You can find a case of it
From the night before

phrases.english: And if it would enter your mind
that one who did not make Kiddush on Shabbat eve
may go on making Kiddush the whole day,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב נָמֵי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לְהוּ
phrases.english: then on Shabbat and Yom Tov day too you can find a case
where there is Kiddush over a cup,
for if he did not make Kiddush at night
he makes Kiddush the next day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in Step 18 challenges Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a missed קידוש is made the next day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That ruling produces a daytime קידוש over a cup, but the ברייתא says there is none.

steps.title: The source does not teach 'what if' cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the ברייתא does not deal with 'what if' cases. It only describes the normal situation, where קידוש was already made at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The ברייתא does not teach cases of 'what if'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends his ruling. The ברייתא is only talking about what usually happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally everyone makes קידוש on Friday night, so normally there is no daytime קידוש over a cup. The case of someone who forgot is unusual, a 'what if' case, so the ברייתא simply did not include it. His ruling therefore still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What if', meaning an unusual case that only happens if something goes wrong
It does not teach

phrases.english: He said to him: It does not teach cases of "what if."

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. He is saying it only describes the usual case, so his ruling about the unusual case does not clash with it.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Steps 18-19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא to the normal case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's statement 'there is no קידוש over a cup by day' covers every situation, even when קידוש was missed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only describes the ordinary situation and leaves out unusual 'what if' cases, so a missed קידוש can still be made by day.

steps.title: רבינא begins a second challenge about honoring the day versus the night
steps.stepSummary: רבינא raises another objection from a ברייתא: if one must choose between honoring the day and honoring the night, honoring the day comes first. If one has only one cup, he says over it... (the text continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: Between the honor of the day and the honor of the night, the honor of the day comes first. And if he has only one cup, he says over it...
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא starts a second challenge against רב נחמן בר יצחק. This step is setup, because the ברייתא is cut off and the actual point comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first gives a general rule: the honor of שבת day comes before the honor of the night. It then turns to someone with only one cup of wine. What he should say over that cup is the key detail, and it continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor of the day, meaning the importance of the daytime שבת meal
The honor of the night, meaning the importance of the Friday-night meal
Comes first, takes priority
One cup (of wine)

phrases.english: He objected to him: The honor of the day and the honor of the night:
the honor of the day takes precedence.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כּוֹס אֶחָד —
phrases.english: And if he has only one cup,
he says over it
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, רבינא brings a second ברייתא against the same ruling from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling that a missed קידוש may be made during the day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. The ברייתא's instruction about the single cup, which appears on the next amud, will be the basis of the challenge.
